title: NSE Launches India’s First Ahimsa Index for Non-Violence-Based Investing
excerpt: The Nifty500 Ahimsa Index, developed with the Ahimsagain Foundation, screens 326 companies from India’s Nifty 500 by their alignment with non-violence principles, excluding firms tied to animal harm, alcohol, tobacco, and weapons.
body:
• NSE Indices launched the Nifty500 Ahimsa Index on July 10, comprising 326 companies from the Nifty 500 screened for non-violence compliance.
  • The index excludes firms involved in meat, dairy, leather, animal testing, alcohol, tobacco, weapons, and gambling under a Green-Orange-Red classification system.
  • Since its base date of April 1, 2016, the index has delivered a 15.11% CAGR, with top holdings including Bharti Airtel, Infosys, and Mahindra & Mahindra.
  • The benchmark is expected to underpin new ETFs and index funds targeting ethical and values-based investors.

NSE Indices Limited, the index services arm of the National Stock Exchange, on July 10 launched the Nifty500 Ahimsa Index — a thematic benchmark that tracks companies from the Nifty 500 universe whose business practices align with the principles of Ahimsa, the Sanskrit term for non-violence.

The index, which currently comprises 326 companies, is designed for investors who want exposure to a diversified basket of large- and mid-cap Indian equities without holding shares in firms linked to animal harm or other activities considered ethically objectionable. It is weighted by free-float market capitalisation and will be rebalanced semi-annually.

How the Screening Works

The index was developed in collaboration with the Ahimsagain Foundation under its Ahimsa Investment Movement (AIM) framework. The AIM system evaluates companies based on how their products, services, and business practices align with non-violence principles, sorting them into three categories.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=MDj7pOULSKg

Companies in the Red band — those significantly involved in meat, dairy, leather, animal testing, alcohol, tobacco, weapons, or gambling — are excluded outright. The Orange band covers firms with more limited exposure to animal-related businesses, such as hotels that serve non-vegetarian food, select FMCG and apparel makers, and most financial companies. Only firms classified as Green, meaning they have minimal or no direct link to animal-harming activities, qualify for inclusion.

"The index offers market participants a transparent, rules-based benchmark that integrates ethical considerations with broad-based equity market exposure."

— NSE Indices

Performance and Composition

Backdated to a base of 1,000 on April 1, 2016, the index has delivered a compound annual growth rate of 15.11% since inception. Over the past five years, it returned a CAGR of 13.09%, though its one-year total return stood at -0.98%, reflecting broader market headwinds.

The largest sector allocations are Automobile & Auto Components at 13.05%, Capital Goods at 12.20%, Information Technology at 11.80%, and Financial Services at 10.35%. Top constituents by weight include Bharti Airtel (6.01%), Infosys (3.74%), Mahindra & Mahindra (2.92%), Tata Consultancy Services (2.21%), and Maruti Suzuki India (1.96%).

The index will be reviewed twice a year using data from January and July. Companies that exit the Nifty 500 or are reclassified into the Red band by the Ahimsagain Foundation can be removed between reviews. Quarterly checks ensure the index meets SEBI's portfolio concentration norms for ETFs and index funds.

Context: Values-Based Investing Gains Ground

The Ahimsa index arrives as values-based and ESG-oriented investing continues to expand globally. India's ethical fund segment, while still modest compared to conventional assets under management, has grown steadily. Tata Mutual Fund launched India's first ethical fund in 1996, followed by Taurus MF in 2009 and Quantum MF in 2024. Industry estimates peg ethical fund AUM at approximately ₹4,000 crore. The Wealth Company Mutual Fund recently launched an Ahimsa-themed ethical fund benchmarked against the Nifty 500 Shariah TRI Index that similarly excludes meat, poultry, and animal-cruelty-linked enterprises.

The Nifty500 Ahimsa Index differs from Shariah-compliant benchmarks in that its screening criteria are rooted specifically in the principle of non-violence toward animals rather than religious financial law, though there is significant overlap in excluded sectors.

What It Means for Diaspora Investors

For members of the Indian diaspora — particularly those in the Jain and vegetarian communities who have long sought investment vehicles aligned with Ahimsa values — the new index offers a formally structured benchmark. While the index itself is not directly investable, NSE Indices said it is expected to serve as the basis for passive investment products including ETFs and index funds, potentially giving NRI investors a route to align their India allocations with ethical preferences.

What's Next

NSE Indices described the launch as part of its broader push to expand its suite of thematic index solutions. Asset managers are expected to evaluate the benchmark for new product launches. The index's semi-annual reconstitution schedule means its next review, using July 2026 data, could adjust the constituent list as companies' practices are reassessed under the AIM framework. Whether fund houses move quickly to launch passively managed products tracking the index will be the key test of investor appetite for non-violence-screened equities.
